MobiScore provides accurate credit scoring from mobile phone usage information, and that it can be a complementary source of data to improve the quality of traditional credit scoring techniques.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using mobile phone data to predict the credit score of users with no prior credit history.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that the usage of mobile phones can be used to predict the credit score of the user, and that this can be used to improve the access to credit for the population that does not have a credit history.
we have demonstrated the possibility to use a non-financial source (mobile phone data) to build a credit scoring model that is as good as a model built from financial history.
we show the feasibility of using mobile phone data as a source of information about financial risk, which can be used to improve traditional credit scoring models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mobile phone data can provide a reliable and universal credit scoring system that can be used to extend credit to the unbanked population, and to improve the credit scoring process for the general population.
mobile phone usage data is a valuable source of information to compute credit scores, and can be used to complement traditional credit scores.
